macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US stocks fall as Alphabet selloff weighs on tech
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.3%, while the Dow declined 0.3% to 52,342.56. Alphabet shares suffered a record-scale decline after disappointing earnings and concerns about sharply higher AI spending.[1][4][8]

items.title: Fed holds rates steady and signals patience
items.summary: The Federal Reserve voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4.00%, citing still-elevated inflation and the need to gather more information before further action. Markets continued to price a potential December move, but the outlook beyond that remained uncertain.[2][6][10]

items.title: US inflation accelerates in September
items.summary: The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.6% year over year in September, up from 3.4% in August and in line with expectations. The data reinforced concerns that inflation remains above the Federal Reserve’s comfort zone.[1][8]

items.title: ECB leaves rates unchanged and keeps December hike in focus
items.summary: The European Central Bank followed the Federal Reserve in holding rates steady, while investors continued to assess the possibility of a December increase amid persistent eurozone inflation risks.[1][9]
items.source: Interactive Investor / Reuters via Galveston County News

items.title: Microsoft beats estimates on strong Azure growth
items.summary: Microsoft reported first-quarter revenue of $92.28 billion, up 19% year over year and above the $90.69 billion consensus. Strong Azure growth supported the results, although device and Windows-license sales weakened amid higher memory and storage costs.[1][3]

items.title: Alphabet disappoints as AI investment drives cash burn
items.summary: Alphabet missed key earnings expectations despite solid cloud performance, while negative free cash flow and plans for much heavier AI infrastructure spending intensified investor concerns. Its shares fell roughly 10%-13%, wiping out close to $400 billion in market value at one point.[3][5][9]
items.source: Tagesschau / Charles Schwab / Reuters via Galveston County News

items.title: Lilly posts strong quarter on GLP-1 demand
items.summary: Eli Lilly reported adjusted third-quarter earnings per share of $7.48 versus the $6.26 consensus, while revenue reached $24.40 billion against expectations of $22.61 billion. Demand for its Zepbound and Mounjaro medicines remained a major growth driver.[10]

items.title: Volkswagen reports major quarterly loss
items.summary: Volkswagen reported a €5.8 billion third-quarter loss, largely reflecting goodwill impairments tied to Porsche. The results underscored continuing pressure on Germany’s automotive sector.[3]

items.title: Samsung profit surges but shares slip
items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported an almost ninefold increase in third-quarter operating profit, but its shares declined after net income narrowly missed analyst expectations.[3]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Binance security incident triggers broad crypto sell-off
items.summary: Binance reported a potential security issue, prompting stablecoin issuers to freeze funds and intensifying market-wide selling. Bitcoin fell to about $77,646, ether to $2,238.76, and BNB declined more than 8% over 24 hours.[1]

items.title: Crypto liquidations surge as Binance exploit rattles markets
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $77,000 while Ethereum, XRP, and BNB also declined; crypto liquidations reached roughly $1.55 billion, mostly involving long positions. Binance said about $3 billion linked to the incident had been frozen and that it would cover user losses.[8]

items.title: Stablecoin issuers freeze funds amid suspected Binance hack
items.summary: Tether and Circle froze significant amounts of stablecoins after Binance disclosed a suspected hack. The full scale of the incident remained unclear while Binance investigated and told users their funds were safe.[3]

items.title: ICE plans U.S. regulated perpetual-futures markets using Hyperliquid infrastructure
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange announced plans to bring perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid infrastructure to the U.S. market, subject to regulatory approvals. Hyperliquid’s HYPE token rose about 14% following the announcement.[6]

items.title: Binance applies for crypto license in Brazil
items.summary: Binance submitted a cryptocurrency-license application in Brazil before the regulatory deadline, beginning a review process that does not guarantee approval.[5]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google reportedly launched Gemini 4 Carbon, which is described as its strongest model and ranks first on the updated Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. The model is initially being directed toward cyber-defense use cases.

items.title: Mistral releases open weights for Large 4
items.summary: Mistral reportedly released the open weights for Mistral Large 4, a roughly 1-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with about 52 billion active parameters, a 1-million-token context window, and text-and-image input.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly prepares IPO filing
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly filed an S-1 registration statement as it prepares for a potential initial public offering, marking a major corporate development for the AI-model company.

items.title: Prime Intellect expands trainable MoE kernel
items.summary: Prime Intellect reportedly released an expanded fused mixture-of-experts kernel based on DeepSeek technology, enabling full model training and aiming to improve training throughput.

items.title: Baseten launches low-cost decision model
items.summary: Baseten reportedly released joey-1, a 2-billion-parameter model designed to return probabilities for decision-making rather than generate conventional text. The company says inference costs are about $0.01 per million tokens.

items.title: NVIDIA introduces offline model for small devices
items.summary: NVIDIA reportedly launched Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, an open model designed to run fully offline on phones and other small devices.

items.title: New York restricts unsafe chatbot behavior involving minors
items.summary: New York enacted restrictions on certain unsafe AI companion features in interactions between chatbots and minors. The law takes effect January 1 and reflects expanding state-level AI regulation in the United States.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Epic Games expands AI-assisted development across Unreal Engine and Fortnite
items.summary: Epic Games says AI coding tools are being used to debug Unreal Engine, identify hardware issues affecting Fortnite, and support development workflows. The company is also publicly discussing broader “vibe coding” practices.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero surpasses 700,000 concurrent Steam players
items.summary: S-Game’s wuxia action game Phantom Blade Zero reportedly exceeded 700,000 concurrent players on Steam shortly after its digital release and topped Steam’s global best-seller chart. A 5GB patch addressed performance issues on PC.

items.title: Bank of America projects GTA 6 PC and multiplayer releases in early 2027
items.summary: A Bank of America analysis reportedly expects a PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 and a new GTA Online experience in early 2027. The projection is tied to Take-Two Interactive’s plans to expand recurring revenue after the console launch.

items.title: Take-Two says gaming is gradually shifting toward PC
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said the industry is moving toward PC and more open platforms, while emphasizing that consoles will remain important for large-scale, big-screen games. Grand Theft Auto 6 is still expected to launch on consoles first.

items.title: Ubisoft outlines future Assassin’s Creed projects
items.summary: Ubisoft provided updates on Assassin’s Creed Hexe, the multiplayer project Invictus, potential remakes, and the franchise’s Netflix adaptation. More information about Hexe is expected next year, while work continues on Invictus.

items.title: NEXUS signs gaming-industry agreement with Dubai Media Council
items.summary: NEXUS announced a strategic memorandum of understanding with the Dubai Media Council to promote gaming-industry development and pursue global business collaboration.

items.title: BioWare co-founder criticizes game-industry executives after studio closure
items.summary: BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk criticized game-industry executives following the reported closure of BioWare by Electronic Arts, arguing that many leaders lack direct game-development experience.
